newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Murdoch says no interest in Fairfax.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Murdoch says no interest in Fairfax.

text.p: Global media operator Rupert Murdoch said on Tuesday that his News Corp Ltd would not take a renewed interest in Australian newspaper publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd now that 25 percent shareholder Conrad Black had sold out.
Black sold his stake on Monday to Brierley Investments Ltd for A$553.8 million.
Asked by an Australian Broadcasting Corp radio reporter in Tokyo why Black had sold, Murdoch said: "He got sick of the aggravation."
Asked if he would again be interested in Fairfax, Murdoch said: "I don't want the same aggravation. I have got enough in my life."
Black cited his problems with ambiguous Australian media regulations as the key reason for the sale.
The Australian government had not allowed Black's Hollinger International Inc to increase its stake to 50 percent.
Murdoch sold his five percent stake in Fairfax last month, leaving Kerry Packer as the remaining media tycoon on the share register with a 14.9 percent holding.
The Australian-born Murdoch, who is now a U.S. citizen, would face the same problems as Black over foreign ownership of Fairfax.
As well, Murdoch would face considerable anti-monopoly "aggravation" because News Corp already controls some 60 percemt of the Australian metropolitan newspaper market.
